problem_meta.agent_answer:
Updated plan:

1. [✓] Decode the first component as a SELFIES molecule.
2. [✓] Identify the aldehyde as the principal reducible group.
3. [✓] Record and validate the predicted transformation.
4. [✓] Report the feasible major product.

## Predicted reaction

The first component decodes to:

```text
COC1=CC=C(CN(CC2=CC=C(OC)C=C2)C3=NC(C)=NC(C4=CC(C=O)=CN=C4NC5=CC=C(OC)N=C5)=N3)C=C1
```

The substrate contains one aldehyde group:

```text
Ar–CHO
```

Under sodium borohydride in methanol/water, followed by ammonium chloride workup, this aldehyde is expected to undergo selective reduction to a primary alcohol:

```text
Ar–CHO  →  Ar–CH2OH
```

## Feasible major product

```text
COC1=CC=C(CN(CC2=CC=C(OC)C=C2)C3=NC(C)=NC(C4=CC(CO)=CN=C4NC5=CC=C(OC)N=C5)=N3)C=C1
```

The transformed fragment is:

```text
C4=CC(C=O)=CN=C4
        ↓
C4=CC(CO)=CN=C4
```

Thus, the expected product is the corresponding heteroaryl methanol. The aromatic and heteroaromatic ring systems are expected to remain unchanged under these mild NaBH₄/NH₄Cl conditions.
